text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache eviction rate > 15% (5m) on prod-cluster-3. Associated continuous-batching latency spike detected. Triggered by recent canary: feature=long-context-prefetch (NTK sliding-window)

Emma O'Connor: I'm on call. Seeing customer-facing p95 token latency climb to ~820ms from 120ms on generator routes. Errors are 502s intermittently. Starting triage.

Raj Patel: thanks emma. I saw the canary rolled last night with adaptive prefetch enabled for the ntk/yaRN families. Could be prefetch creating very large kv footprints and continuous batch backpressure.

Sara Kim: paging infra now. I'll pull the runbook. Possible mitigations: disable prefetch, reduce max_batch_size to 8, toggle sliding-window length to 512.

Lee Torres: support is getting DM's from two customers about slow responses in chat flows. I'll mark their sessions as potentially impacted and open tickets.

Emma O'Connor: priority: keep surface stable for paying customers. Raj, can you push a config rollback for the canary or flip prefetch off for prod-cluster-3?

Raj Patel: doing a scoped toggle (no full deploy). Running command to flip feature flag for prod-cluster-3 canary group.

Raj Patel: command: ```
# toggle prefetch off for canary group
redwoodctl feature set long-context-prefetch --env=prod --cluster=prod-cluster-3 --group=canary --value=false
```

deploy-bot: Deployment event: feature flag updated by raj.patel — long-context-prefetch=false on prod-cluster-3 at 2026-03-15T13:29:45Z

Sara Kim: monitoring whether eviction rate drops. Watching kv-eviction-ratio and continuous-batch-queue-length.

Emma O'Connor: Lee, can you confirm which customers reported issues and whether any are on Dedicated? We should prioritize Dedicated tenants.

Lee Torres: two reports: acct alpha-markets (hosted) and beta-corp (dedicated Europe). Beta-corp experiencing 5xxs. I'm escalating beta-corp to enterprise oncall.

Ana Silva: pinging account team for beta-corp. Also want a quick customer-facing note if we see >10min impact.

Raj Patel: preliminary metrics: after flag flip eviction rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in ~90s. batch queue length fell ~55%. p95 latency trending down to ~180ms but still above baseline.

Sara Kim: good sign. I'll keep the pager open. Next action: reduce max_batch_size on the biggest executor fleet to limit KV pressure. Suggest `max_batch_size=8` (current 32).

Raj Patel: reducing batch size now on prod-cluster-3 executors. Command: ```
redwoodctl runtime update --cluster prod-cluster-3 --pool ntk-exec --set max_batch_size=8
```

deploy-bot: Runtime config updated by raj.patel — ntk-exec max_batch_size=8 at 2026-03-15T13:35:10Z

Emma O'Connor: Any blowback from lower throughput? We might see higher CPU per-token but lower latency. Fine for now to protect customers.

Sara Kim: confirmed: throughput down ~18% but p95 now at 160ms and error spikes gone. eviction ratio stable ~4%.

Lee Torres: beta-corp support contact acknowledged incident and appreciated rapid response. No SLA breach yet.

Ana Silva: please prepare a short incident summary for stakeholders (what, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, customers affected, next steps). I'll draft customer note post-mortem.

Raj Patel: root cause hypothesis: NTK sliding-window adaptive prefetch created high cardinality KV footprints when long-context indexing combined with continuous-batching; this caused KV eviction storms and cascading backpressure, pushing batch latencies and transient 502s. Regression surfaced only under production traffic distribution and batch concurrency.

Sara Kim: next steps: 1) keep prefetch off for canary/prod-cluster-3 2) run stress test with synthetic long-context traces and controlled batch concurrency 3) add guardrail alert: kv-eviction > 10% trigger auto-disable prefetch 4) dev ticket to revisit prefetch memory bounds and sliding-window heuristics.

Emma O'Connor: timeline note: issue detected 13:24 UTC, prefetch toggled off 13:29, batch size reduced 13:35, error spike cleared ~13:37, monitoring until 13:50 — handoff to SRE for post-incident follow-up.

Sara Kim: taking post-incident lead. I'll open incident ticket with logs and add runbook updates. Attaching key logs and sample stack traces to the ticket.

Raj Patel: pulling sample heap profiles and kv-store metrics into the incident ticket now.

Lee Torres: I'll update both customers around status and next steps.

Emma O'Connor: great work team. I'll unassign myself from oncall handoff once Sara confirms follow-up tasks in the ticket. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated — status=mitigated, severity=SEV3, incident_id=INC-20260315-021. Follow-up owner: Sara Kim.

Sara Kim: I'll schedule a 30-min postmortem sync tomorrow to run through reproducer and remediation timeline.

Emma O'Connor: thanks, closing thread from oncall perspective.
